title: Willard Alexander, Milt Ebbins and Joe Glasser
summary: Jones sorts out the managers and bookers around Basie, saying Alexander was the biggest in the business but did not know how to handle a black band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: What about this other manager that you mentioned, Milt Evans or somebody?

This was later. He didn't come in till the 40's. Milt was with MCA, then later he went with William Morris. He became the big man. Mr. Willard Alexander was the biggest man in the promotional business, GAC or what have you. He was the only one that knew because -
Where was Joe Glasser around that time?
Joe had just come into New York and he was

hanging out with cats and he had Louis and what have you. That was a different thing. He did not get into this thing. He did not, you see, Mr. Willard Alexander was the big man. But as I explained to him when I first met him, "Mr. Willard Alexander, you don't know anything about handling a black band. You know about handling a white band." He will tell you to this day that I told him. I told him on several occasions, "You still don't know how to handle a black band."
Later on, in some of these tapes from before, you said he came to you and asked your advice about it.
